title: Lascodia Trading Engine API
source: Generated from the engine's OpenAPI document (Swashbuckle) joined with each action's authorization and rate-limit metadata by ApiReferenceDocumentTests. Do not edit by hand.

endpoints.summary: Change the authenticated admin user's own password.

Log in with a username + password. Every credential failure answers the same; after `Auth:Lockout:MaxFailures` consecutive failures the user is locked for `Auth:Lockout:Minutes` and every attempt answers 429 without the password being checked.
Revoke the bearer token used for this call and clear the auth cookie.
Returns the authenticated admin user's profile, roles and effective permissions.
Silently renew the current admin JWT (body token or `lascodia-auth` cookie). A refused renewal answers 401 (sign in again); 503 when session state could not be read.
List all registered EA instances (fleet view).
Fleet-wide: reset circuit breakers on every live EA instance.
Fleet-wide: clear COMPLIANCE safety-stop on every live EA instance.
Fleet-wide: flatten every live EA instance.
Fleet-wide: kill-switch every live EA instance.
Fleet-wide: lift kill-switch on every live EA instance.
Fleet-wide: in-place restart every live EA instance via ChartApplyTemplate.
Fleet-wide: force SAFETY_STOP on every live EA instance.

Read the candle-stream-source selection (global default + per-symbol overrides) plus the pickable fleet. Candle market data is global per `(Symbol, Timeframe, Timestamp)`; when several EA instances on different brokers own the same symbol their feeds overwrite each other into "duplicate" bars. Designating a single source per symbol makes the ingestion handlers ignore writes from every other instance.
Designate (or clear) the EA instance authorised to stream candles. Omit `symbol` to set the global default; pass a symbol for a per-symbol override. An empty `instanceId` clears the selection.

Ask the EA for a symbol's candle history over a date range (G30) — deeper than its startup backfill. Dry run unless `dryRun = false`: the answer lists the RequestBackfill commands (chunks) it would queue and the instance they go to — the symbol's designated candle source, the only one whose history is stored. The range is capped (`CandleHistory:MaxBarsPerRequest` bars of the timeframe, about 173 days of M1 by default). Received bars are ingested like any backfill: stored bars kept, new ones inserted, soft-deleted slots revived, weekend, off-grid and inconsistent-OHLC bars skipped. `onlyMissing = true` asks only for the slots the stored series lacks (one command per run of gaps, never a slot already asked for). Refused: a range older than the candle retention horizon (`DataRetentionOptions.CandleHotDays`), and anything over the instance's 24-hour budget (`CandleHistory:MaxBarsPerInstancePer24h`). A queued request is recorded in the decision log.

Repair the stored candle history (FIXUP-2 Q8): remove weekend rows (the EA offset fault's +3 h Friday copies), rebuild H4/D1 on the UTC grid from the hourly bars, relabel the pre-coverage D1 labelled a day early. Dry run unless `?dryRun=false`: the default response only reports, per symbol and timeframe, every row it would change and why. `symbols` is a comma-separated list (default: every symbol). Removals are soft deletes; an applied run records the previous prices of every corrected bar in the decision log.

Move the candles the EA stored one hour early to their true UTC open. The EA converted historical broker times with the offset in force when it sent them, so history backfilled in summer that falls in the broker's UTC+2 winter (EU winter time, which includes the weeks between the US and EU clock changes) was stored an hour early. Every FX week of every M1/M5/M15/H1 series is classified — Shifted, LikelyShifted, Correct, Mixed (two offsets in one week), OtherOffset, Ambiguous — from the session edges, the release spikes and the daily rollover; only Shifted weeks move (LikelyShifted too with `includeLikelyShifted=true`), each (symbol, timeframe) in one transaction, audited in the decision log. Dry run unless `?dryRun=false`. H4/D1 are not touched: rebuild them from the corrected H1 afterwards with `POST candles/repair?weekendRows=false&higherTimeframes=true` (the report names the symbols). With `resolveMixed=true` the Mixed weeks are resolved too: a batch stored at another offset (the raw-server-time backfill, +3h in EU summer / +2h in EU winter) loses its copies and moves to its true stamps, and M5/M15/H1 weeks built from that M1 are rebuilt from the resolved M1 (send M1 in the same request). `removeJunkCopies=true` removes copy runs that price continuity proves to be junk.

Repair missing candle volume (engine defect D58): queue EA candle backfills over the range of stored candles whose Volume/TickVolume is missing, addressed to the symbol's designated candle source. The backfill handler then fills only the missing volume fields of bars whose prices agree — prices are never changed. Omit the range to cover every candle with missing volume; pass `dryRun = true` to see the counts and the planned commands only.
List all saved EA config profiles.
Create or update a profile. Unknown knob names are rejected, not silently dropped.
Soft-delete a profile. The name is freed for reuse immediately.
Apply a profile to one or more instances. Partial success is expected and reported per-target: one disconnected EA must not stop the others.
Full detail for one EA instance (includes the rich state envelope).
Safety-audit timeline for one EA instance (newest-first, defaults to 200 entries).

Read the per-EA rule-based breakeven-exit configuration. Two mechanics: salvage exit (close at breakeven after MAE crossed + price returns near entry) and trail to BE (move SL to entry after MFE crossed). Both off by default. Storage is account-scoped; route key is per-instance to match the EA detail page's mental model.

Update the per-EA rule-based breakeven-exit configuration. All thresholds are fractions of the position's SL distance (R-units). Hot-reloads through EngineConfigCache; takes effect on the next PositionWorker cycle without a redeploy.

Snapshot a live instance's EFFECTIVE config into a new profile. Captures what the instance is actually running (post config_override replay), not its chart defaults. Identity and connectivity fields -- instanceId, magicNumber, engineBaseUrl, symbols -- are deliberately excluded.
Reset a tripped circuit breaker (per-symbol, fleet, or both).
Clear a COMPLIANCE-category safety stop.
Hot-reload the EA's safety config (10 knobs; omitted = keep current).

Read the per-EA fill-mode toggle. Controls whether the engine emits the signal's structural entry price on the wire (Limit) or zeroes it so the EA fires at market (Market — default). Hot-reloads through EngineConfigCache; takes effect on the next signal poll without a redeploy.
Update the per-EA fill-mode toggle. Body: `{ "fillMode": "Market" | "Limit" }`. Writes one EngineConfig row keyed `EA:FillMode:{InstanceId}`.
Close every position the EA owns at market. Does not change kill/safety state.
Trigger kill switch: close every position the EA owns and halt new orders.
Phase-9: live log tail for one EA instance (newest-first, defaults to 200 entries).

Read the per-EA pending-signal-reval configuration. When enabled, LLM recommendations whose entry is far from market at signal-generation time (measured in ATR units) are parked in PendingReval status until price reaches the recommended entry — at which point a re-validation LLM call decides whether to promote the signal or kill it. Off by default. Storage is account-scoped; route key is per-instance to match the EA detail page's mental model. Schema-first deferral shipped ahead of the gate + worker that read/mutate it — operators can configure thresholds in advance without yet activating the gate.

Update the per-EA pending-signal-reval configuration. Hot-reloads through EngineConfigCache; takes effect on the next gate/worker cycle without a redeploy. The setting is engine-wide, so only the platform operator may change it: HTTP 403 (`-403`) for another organisation.
Lift a previously-triggered kill switch. Does not re-open positions.
Phase-10: in-place restart via ChartApplyTemplate — picks up a freshly-compiled binary.
Phase-3B: force the EA to drain its persistent HTTP retry queue ASAP.
Phase-3B: delete every pending file in the EA's retry queue (last-resort, unrecoverable).
Force the EA into SAFETY_STOP (default category COMPLIANCE — manual recovery only).
Phase-14: graceful targeted shutdown — the EA closes its own chart, runs OnDeinit, releases symbols, deregisters.
Phase-11: spawn a new EA instance on the same MT5 terminal (one broker account).

Read the per-EA spread-pad toggle. Combined with the engine-wide `SpreadReactive:Pad:Enabled` master under AND semantics: either off skips the pad for this account. Defaults to disabled when no row exists — operator must opt each account in. Hot-reloads through EngineConfigCache.
Update the per-EA spread-pad toggle. Body: `{ "enabled": bool }`. Writes one EngineConfig row keyed `EA:SpreadPad:Account:{accountId}`.
Every organisation's grants (filter by organisation or feed; revoked ones on request).
Grant an organisation a feed (within its plan).
Revoke a grant (kept, marked revoked). Live subscriptions to the feed end within seconds.
Change a grant's usages and validity.
The feeds a grant can name, the default feeds and House's rule.
The exchange usage report of a month: distinct users and organisations per feed, display and non-display.
The month's usage report as CSV: per organisation (`detail=tenants`, default) or per user (`detail=users`).
Every registry row, enabled or not, with the machine identities allowed to write it.
Register an FX venue source (`venue-{venueId}`, feed `venue:{venueId}`), disabled.
Enable/disable an external source, set its writers, display name, symbol map or contract size.

Returns the unified notification feed for the calling operator. Defaults to a 24h window and 100 items. Items are merged from all sources, sorted newest-first, and tagged with the operator's read and mute state so the bell can render badge + visual emphasis without further round-trips.

Updates the calling operator's "last read" high-water mark. Pass `asOfUtc` to use the timestamp visible in the panel when the operator clicked — protects against missing items that arrived after the panel rendered but before the click.
Silences notifications of a specific type-key for the caller for `durationHours` hours. Idempotent — re-muting extends the window to the new end-time when later.
Clears the mute for a specific type-key for the caller.
Which build each role-scoped process is running, and whether they agree.
Per-EA observability — heartbeat staleness + distilled state-envelope highlights.
Engine-side vitals — DB latency, working order/position counts, outbox depth.
Aggregated snapshot across the whole fleet (EAs, daemons, sessions).
Read the engine-wide "convert approved parked recs → live signals" master switch. Global config (not per-instance) — surfaced on the Trade Signals / Parked Recs page.
Set the engine-wide parked-rec → signal conversion switch. Body: `{ "enabled": true|false }`. false = park-for-analysis-only.
Paginated LascodiaTradingEngine.Domain.Entities.PendingSignalRec rows, newest first. Optional symbol substring + state filter. Pass `states=Parked,Revalidating` for the active-only cockpit view.
Operator-initiated cancel of a Parked rec. Returns 409 if the row is already in a non-Parked state (Revalidating in-flight, or terminal).
List all registered daemons with online status + advertised installs.
Daemon registration (idempotent — re-register overwrites). A daemon token may write only its own row; trading-account/EA tokens are refused (403); operators need `access.operator`.

Bootstrap auth for the sidecar daemon. Anonymous endpoint — the daemon proves identity via the API key in the body; engine returns a short-lived JWT it then uses for all subsequent calls. A known `DaemonId` must present its registered key (401 otherwise); a new one is accepted only from a trusted network or with the `X-Daemon-Bootstrap-Token` header (403 otherwise). See LascodiaTradingEngine.Application.Admin.Terminals.AuthenticateDaemonCommand for the security model.
Daemon heartbeat — refresh LastSeenAt + reconcile sessions. Same caller rule as register.
Return the daemon's supervisor.yaml as JSON with sensitive fields (apiKey, engine_token) redacted. Useful for verifying the running config matches operator intent.

List a daemon's advertised installs with the full schema (wine_binary + extra_args) the admin UI's per-row edit form needs. Distinct from M:LascodiaTradingEngine.API.Controllers.v1.AdminTerminalsController.ListDaemons which returns only the summary the dropdown needs.

Clone `/Applications/MetaTrader 5.app` on the daemon's host for a new broker. Bundle ends up at `/Applications/MetaTrader 5 - <slug>.app` with a fresh `CFBundleIdentifier` so macOS provisions a separate Wine prefix. Returns the path the operator should point `register` at after the manual MT5 login dance.

Register an MT5 install with the daemon. The daemon autofills `broker_name` + `account_login` from the install's `config/common.ini`, appends to `supervisor.yaml`, and reloads its in-memory config so the install is immediately launchable.
Remove an install entry from the daemon's supervisor.yaml. Daemon refuses if a running terminal session points at it — operator must close the session first.

Patch one or more fields on an install (sparse update — only the fields actually present in the body are mutated). Useful for fixing a typo'd display name, flipping use_wine, or adding/removing extra_args without re-registering.
Tail the daemon's stderr log. lines defaults to 200; daemon clamps to [1, 2000].

List MT5 terminal64.exe processes running on the daemon's host that the daemon is NOT tracking — pre-daemon manual launches or stale post-crash leftovers. Includes an `installHint` when the orphan's executable path matches one of the configured installs, so the operator knows which broker the stale terminal belongs to.

Terminate one orphan MT5 process by PID. Daemon refuses if the PID belongs to a tracked session (operator must use the regular close-session endpoint), and refuses non-terminal64 PIDs. With `force=true` the daemon skips SIGTERM and goes straight to SIGKILL — appropriate when MT5 is unresponsive.

Trigger the daemon to self-exit so launchd respawns a fresh process. Used after on-disk code updates or to recover from a hung state. Daemon returns 202 immediately + exits 200 ms later; the engine tolerates the resulting connection-reset as a soft success.

Rotate the daemon's `daemon_api_key`. Engine still has the OLD key pinned via TOFU — the response includes the new key + the remediation steps the operator must run (clear the engine row, restart daemon) before normal /auth succeeds again.
Launch a terminal — engine proxies to the daemon's /terminals/launch.
List terminal sessions (optionally scoped by daemonId).
Close a terminal session — engine proxies to the daemon.
List admin users (optional search).
Create an admin user; returns the one-time temporary password. 403 when a role carries a permission the caller lacks.
Update an admin user's profile. 403 for a super admin (unless the caller is one) or a stronger user.
Activate or deactivate an admin user. 403 for a super admin (unless the caller is one) or a stronger user.
Reset an admin user's password; returns the one-time temporary password. 403 for the caller's own account (use change-password), a super admin (unless the caller is one) or a stronger user.
Replace an admin user's role assignments. 403 for the caller's own roles, a super admin (unless the caller is one), a stronger user, or a role carrying a permission the caller lacks.
Create a new alert rule.

Enable or disable an alert channel without touching its credentials. Disabled channels short-circuit in `SendAsync`: nothing is sent and the dispatch log records `Skipped` with the reason (not a failure, never "Sent"). Useful for silencing a channel that's rate-limited or under maintenance without losing its config.
Per-channel configuration status (IsConfigured + masked destination). Destination strings are masked server-side so the UI can render "Configured ✓ — alerts@…" without ever receiving the secrets.

Send a synthetic test alert through one channel. Bypasses dedup/cooldown since the operator is the dedup signal here. Returns 200 with delivered=false when the channel is unconfigured or the SMTP/HTTP call throws.
Paged list of alert rules with optional filters.

A script strategy's alert deliveries (outbox rows), newest first, with each status (Pending, Delivered, Skipped, Failed, Expired), attempts and last error. Read-only; webhook URLs are not returned. `limit` 1-500 (default 50).
Soft-delete an alert rule.
Get a single alert rule by id.
Update an existing alert rule.

What happened on each channel every time this alert was sent, newest first: Sent, Skipped (the channel is switched off or not set up — `errorMessage` says which) or Failed (with the error). Resolutions included; destinations masked. `limit` 1-500 (default 50).
The organisation's e-mail, webhook and Telegram channels (masked), each with where it comes from.
New webhook signing secret (shown once); also stops the deprecated `X-Lascodia-Secret` header.
Removes one channel (House falls back to its platform channel).
Sets up or changes one channel (`email`, `webhook` or `telegram`).
Sends a test alert through one channel of the organisation.
Per-gate ghost efficacy — which gate's rejections would mostly have WON (over-blocking).
Histogram of rejection reasons over a window — which gate blocks the most flow.

One exportable audit trail of everything the agent did that mattered, time-ordered: approvals asked and answered, change sets and their lifecycle steps, graded outcomes, model-lifecycle transitions, engine-config writes, runs, and monitors armed and fired. Defaults to the last seven days. `format=csv` downloads the same rows as CSV.

Has the agent been right before? Predicted vs realised across every graded change, overall and per area, each with a one-sentence bias line a reasoning prompt can paste verbatim — and which says plainly when there is not enough evidence to characterise anything.
List change sets, newest-first — optionally scoped to one work-order conversation.
Record one atomic commit as a durable, chat-reviewable change set (idempotent on Sha).
Record a live measurement against a deployed change's outcome scorecard and re-grade it.
Advance a change set's lifecycle (Approved/Merged/Deployed/RolledBack/Abandoned). Deploying opens the outcome scorecard from the change's experiment prediction.
The curated data dictionary — column semantics the agent reads to interpret engine data.
Arm a watching (tier-0) monitor anchored to a work-order session, so the agent can wait for something that will happen after its run has ended and be woken when it does.

Call one engine operation. A read executes now; a write returns an approval card and executes nothing until a second call carries that card's approved turn id; a denied operation never executes, approval or not.
Describe one operation in full — route params, query params, body shape, access.
Find engine operations the agent could call, with the access level it would get.

The approval policy in force, and every grant currently open: which verbs need two distinct operators, which trading accounts are protected (and whether that list is resolved live or pinned), how long a grant lasts by default, and what is open right now with its reason and remaining minutes.

Open a deliberate, time-boxed window in which the agent may act on ONE protected (live) trading account. Requires a reason, is recorded in the config audit log, replaces any existing window on that account, and closes itself. Returns the whole policy so the operator sees every window now open.
Run a guarded, read-only SQL query (single SELECT) for open-ended data analysis — the QUERY_DATA tool (ADR-0020). Rejects anything but a read-only query; row-capped + timed out.
The agent's own work-order reports across sessions, newest first — what it has already concluded, and where each conclusion was written.
The end-to-end change scorecard — predicted vs realised, per change (ADR-0020 §F).
Open a work-order session (mints the "Engineer" anchor conversation on /conversations).
The newest run on a session — status pill, steps, cost, activity, capabilities and watches for the chat header. `data = null` when the session has never had a run.
The host reports run progress here (upsert by runKey). Only the fields present change.
Stop the run executing on a session — proxied to the host, which owns the run loop.
Append a reasoning / judge / proposal / commit turn to a session, live.
Edit a turn the agent already posted — the plan card as tasks complete, or a tool turn whose result arrived after the call was announced. Assistant/Tool turns only.
Read a session's turns (oldest-first) — the read side of the chat control loop; the agent polls this for operator instructions/approvals. Page with sinceTurnId.

Launch a work order from the UI — proxies to the host algo-engineer service, which runs the OBSERVE→…→PROPOSE loop and streams its Engineer conversation onto /conversations. Returns the anchor conversation id the UI opens; fire-and-forget (the run continues on the host).

Audit events, newest first. Filters (all optional, combined): `from`/`to` (ISO 8601 instants; to is exclusive), `tenantId`, `actor` (an exact actor id such as `admin-user:5`, or text in the actor's name), `actorType`, `action` (key prefix, e.g. `auth.`), `category`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `outcome`. Paging is by cursor: pass the previous page's `nextBeforeId` as `beforeId`; `limit` 1–200 (default 50).

The filtered events as JSON Lines (`application/x-ndjson`, one event per line, oldest first), at most 100,000 per request (header `X-Audit-Export-Limit`); continue with `afterId` = the last line's id. The export itself is recorded in the audit log.

Recomputes the hash chain over `fromId`..`toId` (the whole log when unset; at most `maxRows` rows, default 200,000) and reports the first broken link, or that the range is intact. When rows remain, `truncated` is true and `nextFromId` continues.

Checks published audit chain heads against this database (h8-harden H8.4): send the anchor file as the body (`text/plain` or `application/x-ndjson`, one anchor per line, oldest first, at most 8 MB). Reports lines that do not chain to each other or whose signature fails, a head that moved backwards, and every anchored row whose hash changed or that is gone without a retention anchor — a whole-chain rewrite that `verify` alone cannot see. Send the copy held OUTSIDE this host; the independent check is `tools/audit-anchors/verify_anchors.py`.
Append an immutable decision log entry
Get paged list of decision logs

Generates a signed JWT token for local development and testing. Returns 404 unless M:LascodiaTradingEngine.API.Authorization.DevTokenEndpointGate.IsAllowed(Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.IConfiguration,Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext,System.String@) passes.
List every per-knob auto-apply config. There are at most a handful of rows (one per tunable knob) so paging is unnecessary.
Soft-delete a per-knob auto-apply config. After delete the worker treats the knob as having no config — auto-apply disabled, operator-only review.
Fetch one per-knob auto-apply config by key. Returns 404-style "-14" when no row exists for the key — operator UI can distinguish "no config yet" from "config disabled."

Upsert a per-knob auto-apply config. Creates the row when absent, updates in place when present. Operator-only — flipping `AutoApplyEnabled` is a high-blast-radius action (turns on autonomous mutation of a production knob).
List auto-tune proposals. Defaults to Pending so the most common query — "what's awaiting my review?" — is the bare endpoint.
Apply a Pending proposal — transactionally upserts the underlying `EngineConfig` row, flips the proposal status to Applied, and records the operator's identity on the proposal + audit log.
Reject a Pending proposal. Does NOT touch `EngineConfig`; just flips status to Rejected with reviewer attribution.
Queue a new backtest run against an existing strategy. Returns the run id; status flips through Queued → Running → Completed/Failed asynchronously via the BacktestWorker.
Get paged list of backtest runs
Get backtest run by Id. Includes the typed mark-to-market equity/drawdown curve (`EquityCurve`) alongside the full `ResultJson`.

Download a completed run as a TradingView-style report — performance summary (all / long / short) and list of trades. `format=csv` (default) or `format=xlsx`. A run that is missing or not completed returns the usual response envelope instead of a file.

Monte Carlo of a completed run's trades in R (BT-I6): P5/P50/P95 of max drawdown, CAGR, total return and time to recover, risk of ruin and probability of loss, from block-bootstrap resamples of the run's R multiples under fixed-fractional sizing. Query: iterations (100–20,000, default 2,000), riskPerTradePct (default 1), ruinDrawdownPct (default 50), seed. -11 with fewer than 10 trades that carried a stop.
Keycloak returns here: the session is created and the browser goes back to the sanitised return path.
Starts a sign-in: 302 to Keycloak (code + PKCE). `acr=mfa` = step-up (sign in again with a second factor).
Ends the session (and, through the returned URL, the Keycloak session). Always clears the cookie.
The signed-in session (C3.1 shape); 401 when there is none.
Moves the session to another organisation the person is an active member of; answers the new session.

A single-use, 30-second ticket for one SignalR connection: connect to `/api/hubs/…?ticket=` with the WebSockets transport and negotiation skipped (the ticket is spent on the first request that presents it).

Screening gate binding-constraint diagnostic. Identifies which gate rejected the most candidates in the lookback window and suggests a targeted tuning direction. Primary consumer: operator-driven threshold tuning decisions — "which gate do I loosen first?"
Paged list of signal rejection audit entries. Filter by stage / reason / symbol / strategy / trade-signal / time window.
Paged list of monthly calibration snapshots. Filter by stage / reason / granularity / period window.

Latest-month-vs-baseline calibration trend report. The primary artifact for quarterly recalibration review: anomalies are surfaced first, followed by high-volume gates. Query params control the baseline length (default 3 months), anomaly threshold (default 15 percentage points), and minimum baseline volume (default 30).
The caller's alerts, newest first; optional symbol / status / kind filters.
Create an alert (armed at once).
The fire log across the caller's alerts (optionally one symbol), newest first.
Delete an alert (its fire log is kept until the retention purge).
One of the caller's alerts.
Replace an alert; editing re-arms it.
One alert's fires, newest first, with each channel's outcome. `limit` 1-500 (default 50).
Stop watching an alert (kept, resumable).
Arm a paused, fired-once or expired alert again (same checks as creating it).
Create a new annotation. Author is taken from the caller's token.
Paged list of annotations for a target chart.
Soft-delete an annotation. Author-only.
Edit the body of an existing annotation. Author-only.

Save and delete drawings one by one, each against the version (`baseUpdatedAt`) it was made from (DR-I3). Per-write outcomes: `00` applied, `-409` stale (with the server's current row), `-11` refused. Applied changes push `chartDrawingsChanged` { symbols, origin }.

Every drawing the caller owns on one symbol (DR-I2), with its effective visibility; with a resolution, only those created on it (the per-chart read of consoles from before drawings were kept per symbol).

Replace the caller's drawing set for one chart. Idempotent: drawings absent from the payload are soft-deleted, and only on this chart. Superseded by M:LascodiaTradingEngine.API.Controllers.v1.ChartDrawingController.Sync(LascodiaTradingEngine.Application.ChartDrawings.Commands.SyncChartDrawings.SyncChartDrawingsCommand); kept for consoles from before it.
The order-book heatmap of [from, to): buckets equal buckets (1..800, default 400), each the LAST order-book snapshot captured inside it; buckets without one are omitted. One broker's MT5 DOM.

Tick flow per chart bar: quote counts, tick-rule delta and running delta, spread range, tick rate and optionally a footprint, aligned to the chart's own bar open times. A POST because the bar times do not fit a query string.
The chart scripts the operator can use (with sources): their own and every shared one (`ownedByMe` tells them apart), most recently changed first.

Save a chart script as version 1 (body: name, pineSource, inputs?, visibility?, note?, and for an import from TradingView sourceUrl, licence?, author?). It must compile and declare indicator() or strategy(); failures return -11 with the compile response as data.

Fetch an open-source TradingView script (body: url — its script page, or a `PUB;…` publication id) for the editor to open as an unsaved draft. Nothing is stored. Refused (-11) for other hosts, protected or invite-only scripts and licences that forbid reuse; -14 when TradingView has no such script.
Delete (soft) a chart script (owner only); its versions are kept with it.
One chart script with its source (the operator's own, or a shared one).

Replace a chart script's name, source and inputs (owner only; recompiled like a create) and record the next version. Send the `revision` the edit started from as `expectedRevision`: a save made on an older revision is refused with -409 instead of overwriting the newer state.
A chart script's versions, newest first, without their sources (limit 1–200, default 100).
One version of a chart script with its source.
Make an older version the script's current state (owner only; body: expectedRevision?). The restored state is recompiled and saved as the next version, so the state it replaces stays in the history.
Share a chart script with every operator, or make it private again (body: visibility; owner only).
The operator's layouts (no state), the active one first.
Create a layout (body: name?, state?, activate = true).
The active layout with its state (null data when there is none yet).
Delete (soft) a layout; deleting the open one opens the most recently used other.
One layout with its state.
Rename and/or replace the state (body: name?, state?, expectedVersion?). A stale expectedVersion → -409 + current layout.
Make a layout the open one.
Copy a layout (body: name?) and open the copy.
Every chart preference of the operator.
Remove one preference.
Set one preference (body: { value }).
The operator's notes — on symbol, or all — pinned first, then newest (no pictures).
Write a note (body: symbol, text, timeframe?, title?, bias? Long|Short, snapshotDataUrl?, layoutId?, isPinned?).
Delete (soft) a note.
One note with its chart picture.
Edit a note: null fields unchanged, "" clears an optional one; clearLayout removes the layout link.

What is live for the accounts in tradingAccountIds (comma-separated; every account when omitted) and the charted symbol: open positions, working orders, live signals and open paper trades — signals and paper trades engine-wide.

Sentiment for the pair's two currencies: the engine's news pressure (−1 … +1, with the change over 24 h) and the latest CFTC positioning of each currency's future. There is no broker retail-positioning feed; the answer says so.
The caller's watchlists by SortOrder; a seeded default (id 0) when they have none.
Create a watchlist.
Soft-delete a watchlist.
Update name / sections / active flag / sort order / display settings. Null fields are unchanged.
The latest basis (age, stale flag) and the per-minute series of the window (default the last 2 h).
Delta / CVD / footprint bars, trade bubbles, large lots, sweeps, iceberg-like levels and absorption.

Phase 5 follow-up — every currently-Active CompositeML policy snapshot, one row per `(Symbol, Timeframe, IsColdStart)` partition tier. Each entry exposes the trainer that wrote it, when it activated, and the per-knob delta JSON so a UI can render "knob X moved by +0.05 since last activation". The screenshot that went with one chat turn, as an image. Sets the FLEET-WIDE execution mode: Off, Shadow or Live.

Architectures the host can actually train, plus the operator-configured auto-pick blocklist. Recently ingested articles with their labels. The raw record layer — use it to check what a feed is actually delivering and how the classifier read it.

Recomputes liveness for roll-up rows written before it was tracked, so the history chart has something to draw. Point-in-time honest — see the command's own documentation, which is the load-bearing part. Bounded per call; repeat while `remainingRows` is non-zero.

Every `NewsIntel:` config row — key, current value, type and the description that explains what the knob does. Scoped to the prefix so the cockpit does not have to pull the engine's entire config table to render one panel.

The focused read for one instrument — exactly the block the analysis prompt would carry, plus whether it would actually carry it and why not. Articles first seen per hour, split by discovery channel. Does `liveShare` actually predict? Buckets closed trades by the live share of the pressure reading in force when they OPENED, split by whether the trade agreed with the news, and compares realised R.
Current (or historical) weighted pressure per currency, with the contributing headlines.

Ingestion and classification health: article counts by status and by source over the window. This is where a silently dead feed shows up — a source whose count went to zero looks exactly like a quiet news day in the pressure score alone.
Pressure history for one currency — the roll-up time series behind the chart.

Every tracked currency's pressure history in one call. Per-currency requests would be nine round trips for one screen, and — worse — nine independently-sampled series. Stop a script strategy's paper-only stage: PaperTrading → Draft (its paper executions are kept). Refused (`-11`) for any other stage except Draft, which answers at once as already stopped.

Arms a monitor that files the stored card when price comes near its entry (default 0.5 ATR short of it), so it rests at the broker before the touch. Body (optional): `{ "mode": "direct" | "confirm", "expiresInHours": 24, "nearAtrFraction": 0.5 }`.

Files the stored card as a signal now, through the normal risk gates. Refused when it is no longer the trade it was (already filed, overtaken by price, too old, refused by a gate).

Manually create a trade signal. The strategy workers create signals automatically; this endpoint exposes the same command path so an operator can hand-author a signal from the admin UI (or curl) — useful when the auto-pipeline is down, when validating a hypothesis before deploying a strategy, or when overriding the engine's silence with a tactical entry. The signal is persisted in `Pending` status and goes through the normal approve/reject/expire workflow; ML scoring fields are typically left null for hand-authored signals.

Full internal state of the signal module: the generate → approve → serve → attempt → fill funnel, every account's readiness to act, and a per-signal matrix showing what each account did with each signal — or precisely what stopped it.

Paged list of LLM signal-review journals — the per-signal post-mortems the engine writes when a signal resolves (traded to TP/SL, or a never-traded ghost outcome). Each row links to the full journal conversation (`ReviewLlmInvocationId`) on the /conversations page. Optional filters: symbol, outcome (Win/Loss/Breakeven/Expired/ EntryNotReached), outcomeKind (Traded/Ghost), status (Pending/Completed/Failed), and a specific signal.

On-demand: (re)generate the LLM journal for a specific signal. Same path the automatic event handler + walker use, exposed for testing and manual re-runs. Idempotent by default — a signal that already has a completed journal returns the existing conversation id without a fresh model call. Pass `force=true` to regenerate anyway (retires the old conversation and makes a new model call) — use after a scoring/prompt fix. Works for traded and never-traded (ghost) signals.
Get paged list of trade signals

Submits a manual order ticket (SP-I4). Judged again by the dry run at submission and refused (-11, reason in `message`) unless every blocking check passes. `mode` "Paper" (the default) opens a paper trade — nothing reaches the broker. "Live" creates a TradeSignal with source Manual of the account's manual-trades strategy (bound to that account only); it then goes through Tier 1 and, at the account's EA, Tier 2, like any signal. Live on a Real account needs `ManualTrading:LiveOnRealAccounts`.
Get approved trade signals pending broker execution

Dry run of a manual order ticket (SP-I4, the chart's Buy/Sell ticket). Prices the ticket for one account — lots from the account's risk profile, the ATR stop guard, spread, swap, risk and reward in money, the exposure after the trade — and runs every check the live path would: the account's safety state (EA, kill switches, emergency halt, drawdown recovery), the news blackout, Tier 1 and a Tier-2 risk check against the account's book. Read-only: nothing is created, sent or recorded. `canSubmit` says whether `POST trade-signal/manual` would accept it now, and `refusedReason` why not.

"What-if" analysis: replay historic signals against actual subsequent candles to compute outcomes under hypothetical TP/SL multipliers. Returns aggregate KPIs at the operator-chosen (tp, sl) point, a sweep table of KPIs across multiple TP multipliers (sl fixed), and per-signal drill-in detail. Drives the Signal Sensitivity Analysis admin page.

Walks a SINGLE proposed/actual (entry, SL, TP, direction) setup forward through real historical candles from `FromUtc` and resolves the outcome — HitTP / HitSL / Expired / EntryNotReached — plus fill time, exit, MFE/MAE in pips, bars-to-exit, and realized R-multiple. The single-signal counterpart to sensitivity-analysis.

Approve a pending trade signal

Cancel a trade signal. The signal becomes Cancelled — terminal, never served, approved or executed again — and every open position it opened is closed and every pending/working order created from it is cancelled, on every account, immediately. Works from any status (an Executed signal's positions are closed). Idempotent: calling it again re-sweeps any position or order that could not be reached the first time (e.g. its EA was offline). Body (optional): `{ "reason": "why" }`.

EA-initiated rejection for a signal it cannot execute (lot-size validator, circuit-breaker, account-profile cap, broker-side limit, etc.). Uses the same MediatR command as the operator-facing /reject route but lives under the EAIngest auth policy so the EA's account-bound JWT can post it. Without this, EA-side rejections leave the signal stuck as Approved in the DB until natural expiry (~30min), and the UI keeps showing actionable signals the EA has already added to its dedup buffer.
Expire a trade signal

EA-initiated local rejection record — pure observability. Unlike `/{id}/execution-rejection` which flips the signal to `Rejected` globally, this endpoint records the rejection event without changing signal status, so other EAs (different brokers / accounts) can still try the same signal. Every EA-local gate (staleness, adverse drift, safety gates, validator, give-up after consecutive engine errors, broker retcode) emits one row. See `docs/SIGNAL_REJECTION_VISIBILITY.md` for the canonical taxonomy of `SubStage` values.

Operator override that flips a Rejected signal back to Pending so it re-flows through Tier-1 risk checks. Used when the viability gate (or any rejection path) dropped a recommendation the operator believes is actionable after all. Original rejection reason is preserved in the column with an audit marker; status flip publishes the integration event so SignalOrderBridgeWorker picks it up. Idempotent for already-Pending / Approved signals; refuses to flip terminal states (Filled / Expired / Cancelled).
Reject a pending trade signal

List rejection events for a single signal — drives the "Account attempts" panel on the Trade Signal detail page. Returns every EA / engine / broker rejection that mentioned this signal, across all accounts.

Revokes the bearer token used to make this call. After logout the same JWT cannot be reused, even before its natural expiry. Idempotent.

Mints a fresh JWT from the currently-presented one without forcing a re-login. !:AllowAnonymous because the previous token may already be past its `exp` — manual signature + jti-revocation + grace-window checks happen inside the handler, so an expired-but-not- revoked token from a laptop that slept past the natural expiry can still recover its session (within `Auth:Refresh:ExpiredGraceMinutes` of its `exp`, never past `auth_time + Auth:Refresh:MaxSessionDays`). On success the old `jti` is revoked (preventing parallel-device replay) and the new token is written back to the `lascodia-auth` cookie for web sessions. A refused renewal answers 401 (sign in again); 503 when session state could not be read.

Register a new trading account and auto-login. For an account that already exists, credentials are returned only against proof of control (API key, API-key blob or password — answered as a login) or to a caller on a trusted network; anyone else gets 403.

Lightweight identity probe. Returns the account id + role claims for the currently authenticated caller. Used by the admin UI on boot to decide whether to show the login screen when the bearer token lives in an HttpOnly cookie the browser can't read.

Mints a short-lived JWT for the SignalR WebSocket handshake. Browsers can't attach HttpOnly cookies to cross-origin WebSocket upgrades in all transports, and the `access_token` query-string fallback requires a readable bearer — so we trade the cookie for a 60-second ticket here. Only usable during the handshake; once the connection is up, SignalR keeps it alive without re-presenting the ticket.

List every viability gate with its current mode, all tunable thresholds, today's firing count, and ghost-outcome breakdown. Stats window is the trailing 24h.

Current GhostOutcomeWorker config (poll cadence / lookback / walk window / per-cycle cap / min-age gate / master switch) — each field returned with its current value plus the compile-time default the UI shows as a Revert hint.

Update one or more GhostOutcomeWorker knobs. Every field is optional — null fields are left untouched; non-null fields are validated and upserted into `EngineConfig`. Worker re-reads the config at the top of every cycle so changes propagate without a restart.

Trigger an on-demand ghost-outcome resolution cycle. Replays unresolved rejected SpotAnalysis signals against subsequent candles and persists the would-have outcomes — refreshes the per-gate ghost-stats block returned by `GET /viability-gates` without waiting for the worker's natural 5-minute poll.

A completed walk-forward run analysed (BT-I5): out-of-sample folds stitched into one equity curve and trade list, walk-forward efficiency (re-optimising runs), and per-fold parameter drift. -11 while the run has not completed.

Monte Carlo in R (BT-I6) of a completed walk-forward run's stitched out-of-sample trades — the most honest trade sample there is: P5/P50/P95 of max drawdown, CAGR, total return and time to recover, risk of ruin. Query as `GET backtest/{id}/monte-carlo`.
